title: Treasury Sanctions Cartel-Linked Casinos and Key Associates on U.S.-Mexico Border
summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's OFAC sanctioned six targets, including two casinos (Casino Centenario and Diamante Casino) operated by CAMSA, linked to Cartel del Noreste (CDN), a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization. The action targets CDN's money laundering operations and its control over human smuggling and drug trafficking along the U.S.-Mexico border near Laredo, Texas, the busiest land port of entry.
key_points: OFAC designated Casino Centenario and its operator CAMSA, both used by CDN to launder illicit proceeds and stash fentanyl pills and cocaine
Diamante Casino (operated by CAMSA) is also designated, with locations in Tampico and an online gambling website
Eduardo Javier Islas Valdez designated as CDN human smuggling gatekeeper controlling migration flows across the Rio Grande into Texas
Defense attorney Juan Pablo Penilla Rodriguez designated for facilitating CDN leadership communications from Mexican prison
This is OFAC's third action targeting CDN during the Trump Administration, following designations on May 21, 2025 and August 6, 2025
CDN was designated as an FTO by the State Department on February 20, 2025
why_it_matters: This sanctions action targets financial infrastructure of one of Mexico's most violent cartels (CDN). While not a direct market catalyst, it affects cross-border trade flows through the Laredo port of entry and reinforces Treasury's enforcement posture against cartel financial networks. The targeting of casino-based money laundering operations could have minor implications for gaming sector compliance and cross-border dynamics.
macro_context: The sanctions target CDN's control over the busiest inland point of entry for U.S. trade. This is a law enforcement action rather than a macro catalyst. Any implications for trade flows through Laredo or MXN/USD would be indirect and negligible relative to broader macroeconomic factors.
